Subject: CoralWave technical alignment: SLOs, model requirements & deployment map

Hi Alyssa / Tom —

Thanks again for the call earlier — solid conversation and lots to unpack. Below is a concise recap of the pain points, goals, and what we discussed for the follow-up technical deep-dive so everyone is aligned. Please correct anything I missed.

Summary of pain / goals
- Tail latency spikes during batch ingestion windows (peak 18:00–20:00 PT) causing generation 95p to jump to ~400ms.
- Need predictable interactive user experience: target 95th <= 150ms for single-shot generation (4k context) and p99 guidance for burst handling.
- Throughput target: baseline 200 qps sustained, ability to absorb 1.5–2x burst for 10–15 minute windows.
- Data controls: SOC 2 + VPC isolation are must-haves for Prod.
- Model requirements: mix of an open 7B-ish base with a narrow finetune for domain intents; want to avoid accuracy degradation from heavy quantization.

Proposed topology notes (from today's talk)
- Hybrid deployment: Dedicated capacity for core traffic in us-west with hosted fallbacks in us-east for DR.
- KV/prefix caching to cut repeated context costs for chat-like flows.
- Autoscale policy: pre-warmed burst pools + fast ramp for 2x short bursts.

Requested artifacts for the technical deep-dive
- P90 / P95 latency traces for at least two production days (include request size / token counts).
- A sample of typical prompts + expected output length distributions.
- Current concurrency profile (avg vs peak) and any queuing you observe.
- Current model spec and whether you can accept int8 vs int4 quantization tradeoffs for lower cost.

Attachments: I attached a draft SLO spreadsheet and a one-page MOP draft to accelerate the convo.

Next steps
- Can we schedule a 60–75 minute deep-dive with your infra/ML engineer and our serving runtime & infra leads? Grace / Irene will join to cover topology and failure modes.
- If you can, please drop the artifacts above into the HubSpot deal link (I've added a folder) before the call.

Thanks — available for a quick sync if you want to triage before the longer call.

—Sean

Looping in a couple of infra/ops items so we come prepared for the deep-dive.

Grace notes / prep list for the call
- Please bring a sample of production requests divided by token footprint (0-512, 513-1024, 1025-4096). This helps size KV cache and batch windows.
- Export a short trace with request timestamps so we can compute effective concurrency over rolling 1-min and 5-min windows.
- If you have a typical traffic replay or small capture, send that (anonymized) so we can run quick local perf tests.
- Confirm whether your finetune is applied server-side (on inference) or as a pre-processing step — this changes memory footprint.

Technical takeaways from our side
- For 95p <=150ms at 4k with 200 sustained qps, our conservative topology suggestion: 4 dedicated GPU instances (A100-like) with continuous batching + prefix caching; warm burst pool of 2 instances for spikes. We'll validate with replay.
- If finetune is small (delta weights) we can serve as a side-loaded adapter to reduce memory pressure. If it's a full-model finetune, we'll need larger memory-tier instances.
- Quantization plan: test int8 first; evaluate LM perplexity and task-specific accuracy vs int8 baseline before considering int4 for cost reasons.

I'll draft a meeting agenda and share a calendar invite (60–75 min). Irene, can you prepare a list of kernel/quantization questions we should answer on the call?

—Grace
